title: What If Mars's Moon Phobos Is Falling Apart?

scenes.text: What if Mars's moon is falling toward it? Mars will get rings.
Phobos is moving closer to Mars by a few centimeters every year.
Eventually it will reach the point where Mars's gravity pulls harder on one side than the other.
In roughly 20 to 70 million years, depending on the model, Phobos will break apart.
The debris will spread into a ring that may last about 100 million years.
Later, the ring could clump into new tiny moons. Mars would go from two moons to a ringed planet.

description:
What if Phobos falls apart and gives Mars rings?
Models predict it will break up within tens of millions of years, and the ring could last around 100 million years.
